staged_source_snapshot.description: Stage 01 reproduced against this staged vulnerable worktree. Its line map matches the saved ASan frames (`encoding.c:539`, `readclause.c:174`, `readclause.c:610`) even though sample metadata names vulnerable commit `2a7080f411cb84b6f6ef5643ccdfe20a0c85f3b2`; the staged snapshot still contains the same unguarded post-tag `c2 = GetC();` hunk that `patch.diff` fixes.

bug_description.original: A malformed tag like <foo in SSML parsing causes espeak to read past the end of the string, resulting in an out-of-bounds read.
bug_description.original_source: sample_info.json issue description / staged patch.diff / staged sanitizer_trace.txt / reproduction_report.json / staged vulnerable worktree `_work/src/espeak-ng`
bug_description.normalized: The staged witness is the exact two-byte file `<w`. The libFuzzer harness copies those bytes into a heap buffer, appends a NUL terminator, and calls `espeak_Synth()` with UTF-8 and SSML parsing enabled, so the vulnerable parser sees the three-byte string `<w\0`. In `ReadClause()`, the leading `<` plus alphabetic lookahead `w` makes the input enter the SSML-tag path. The tag-scan loop copies `w`, then consumes the appended NUL and reaches EOF without ever seeing `>`. `ProcessSsmlTag()` returns `0` for the unknown tag name `w`, so vulnerable `ReadClause()` falls through to the post-tag `c2 = GetC();` fetch even though EOF has already been reached. `GetC()` forwards the at-end decoder into `string_decoder_getc_utf_8()`, whose first statement dereferences `*decoder->current++` and performs the 1-byte heap out-of-bounds read reported by ASan. The fix adds the missing `if (!Eof()) { c2 = GetC(); }` guard after SSML tag processing.

source.description: First project parser read on the vulnerable path. With SSML mode enabled, `ReadClause()` consumes the first byte of the staged string into lookahead `c2`, materializing the `<` opener that later enters SSML-tag parsing.
source.value_from: The staged `poc` has SHA-256 `37fcafd28fb4481c72f67e0b9f22f12b09c558ecdde456908ec2d585197a0010` and exact bytes `3c 77` (`<w`). `tests/ssml-fuzzer.c` copies those two bytes to a heap buffer, appends `0x00`, and passes the resulting three-byte UTF-8 string `<w\0` to `espeak_Synth()` with `espeakSSML` enabled.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

sink.description: ASan sink. The UTF-8 decoder dereferences `decoder->current` after `ReadClause()` has already advanced it to `decoder->end`, so the read lands exactly one byte past the `<w\0` heap buffer.
sink.note: Both `sanitizer_trace.txt` and `reproduction_report.json` report the crash at `src/libespeak-ng/encoding.c:539:15` in `string_decoder_getc_utf_8()` as a 1-byte heap-buffer-overflow read.

root_cause.description: Root cause. After SSML tag scanning has already consumed the appended NUL and reached EOF because no closing `>` was present, `ReadClause()` still fetches a post-tag character unconditionally instead of checking `!Eof()` first.
root_cause.note: The staged fix in `patch.diff` repairs this exact obligation by changing the vulnerable tail to `if (!Eof()) { c2 = GetC(); }`.

tainted_value_origin.description: The harness materializes the exact two-byte witness as a heap string, appends one NUL terminator, and submits that three-byte buffer to espeak with `espeakCHARS_UTF8 | espeakPHONEMES | espeakSSML`.

parser_admitted.description: With `c1 == '<'` and `c2 == 'w'`, the malformed witness is admitted to the SSML tag parser instead of being treated as ordinary text.

fine_trace.note: Source. `ReadClause()` reads the first byte of the staged `<w\0` string into lookahead `c2`. On the witness that byte is `0x3c` (`<`), the opener for the later SSML-tag branch.

At the top of the first loop iteration, `c1` becomes the previously read `<`. The same iteration then executes line 548 to read the second witness byte into `c2`, producing `c2 == 'w'`. The line-550 EOF fallback does not fire yet because the decoder still points at the appended NUL byte, not `end`.
Because SSML mode is enabled, `c1 == '<'`, and `iswalpha(c2)` is true for `w`, the parser treats the bytes as an SSML tag start and enters the tag-parsing block.

Starting with `c1 == 'w'`, the loop copies that byte into `xml_buf[0]`, then `c1 = GetC()` consumes the appended NUL terminator. No `>` was seen before that read, so the loop exits with `xml_buf` containing only `w` and the decoder positioned at EOF.

fine_trace.code: terminator = ProcessSsmlTag(xml_buf, buf, &ix, n_buf, xmlbase, &audio_text, voice_change, &base_voice, base_voice_variant_name, &ignore_text, &clear_skipping_text, &sayas_mode, &sayas_start, ssml_stack, &n_ssml_stack, &n_param_stack, (int *)speech_parameters);
fine_trace.note: With `xml_buf` equal to `w`, `ProcessSsmlTag()` resolves an unknown tag name and returns `0`. As a result, the `if (terminator != 0)` early return at lines 604-607 is skipped and control falls through to the vulnerable post-tag fetch.

Root-cause step. Even though step 4 already left the decoder at EOF and step 5 returned `terminator == 0`, `ReadClause()` unconditionally asks for one more character after the malformed tag. The patch fixes this by guarding the call with `if (!Eof())`.
`GetC()` has no separate EOF guard once it is called. The at-end decoder from step 6 is forwarded directly to the active text-decoder backend, which is the UTF-8 reader on this harness path.
Sink. `string_decoder_getc_utf_8()` dereferences `decoder->current` even though it already equals `decoder->end`, producing the ASan 1-byte read exactly 0 bytes past the 3-byte `<w\0` heap region.

format.name: raw-utf8-ssml-input
format.contract: The witness is the exact two-byte UTF-8 file `3c 77` (`<w`). The libFuzzer harness appends one NUL byte and calls `espeak_Synth()` with `espeakSSML`, so `ReadClause()` sees the three-byte string `<w\0`, enters the SSML-tag path, reaches EOF before any closing `>`, and then executes the vulnerable post-tag `GetC()`.
